counterargs.read: The relief rally extends and broadens for a second session: equity vol keeps compressing (VIX -1.41%) and the Korea gate holds open with widening margins, while credit proxies mostly firm and belly/long-end yields ease further. But DFII5's firming to 2.55% is the more important signal per the real-rate hierarchy -- real yields are rising even as nominal yields ease, which is a genuinely different read than a simple 'conditions easing' story. Combined with MOVE's third straight session above 80, this still reads as short-term conditions holding within a structurally restrictive backdrop -- improving at the margin, not yet confirming a regime shift. The 2Y/5Y/7Y coupon trio this week (today's 2Y results still pending) is the next real test of whether Treasury demand is holding up broadly, not just in the reopenings seen so far this month.

mmf.government_fund_aum_note: Government/Treasury funds are the largest MMF subclass by AUM. This is a buyer-BASE size, not a measure of actual Treasury securities held -- government funds also hold repo (often Treasury-collateralized but not itself a Treasury security) and agency debt.
mmf.treasury_holdings_note: The ICI weekly release does not break out direct Treasury bill/note/bond holdings within government funds separately from repo and agency exposure. Actual $ of Treasury securities held by MMFs is not yet wired into this pipeline.
mmf.net_treasury_purchases_note: Marginal net Treasury purchases by MMFs this week cannot be measured from AUM changes alone. Not fabricated -- shown as PENDING until a flow-based source (e.g., Treasury OFR MMF holdings detail, or SEC N-MFP) is integrated.
